subject: Materials Science
title: Alumina: The Workhorse Ceramic
description: Learn Alumina: The Workhorse Ceramic in one minute.

hook.text: Hip replacement joints, spark plugs, and armor plates all use the same ceramic — alumina.

buildup.text: Alumina is aluminum oxide — cheap, hard, and chemically inert up to 1,700°C.

discovery.text: Its hardness is second only to diamond among oxides, making it ideal for grinding wheels.

twist.text: Ruby and sapphire are just alumina with trace impurities — precious gems from a common oxide.

climax.text: More alumina ceramic is produced than all other advanced ceramics combined.

punchline.text: The humblest oxide makes rubies and stops bullets.

quiz.question: What are rubies and sapphires chemically?
